Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis MedTech Inc. Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO; Maria Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis MedTech demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance: new product launches and their contribution to growth; gross margin trends and supply chain dynamics; capital equipment versus consumables mix trends; the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives; R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress; overall performance highlights and key achievements; and the key assumptions underlying our guidance.

Maria will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Tom will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with new product launches and their contribution to growth.

I'm thrilled to highlight one of the standout drivers of our record performance this year. We've prioritized innovation in the medical devices arena, where the global market is set to expand at a 5.2% CAGR through 2028 according to Grand View Research, propelled by aging populations, the rise of minimally invasive procedures, and the integration of digital health solutions. Our disciplined R&D execution, investing 11.8% of revenue this year compared to 10.2% last year, has enabled us to seize substantial market share in fast-growing areas such as structural heart, neuromodulation, and precision diagnostics.

On a broad scale, products launched within the past 24 months represented 28% of our total FY 2023 revenue, rising from 19% in FY 2022, and they fueled 32% year-over-year organic growth portfolio-wide. In Q4 specifically, these innovations generated $187 million in sales, reflecting a remarkable 45% YoY surge that tripled the pace of our core business. Beyond revenue, this represents premium growth, with gross margins on these new items reaching 72%, or 450 basis points above our overall average, supported by strong pricing power, efficient scalable production, and positive reimbursement trends in value-based care environments.

Diving into specifics, our VitalFlow™ TAVR System, our advanced transcatheter aortic valve replacement platform, led the charge. It earned FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in Q2 2023 and boasts a repositionable, low-profile design incorporating AI-enhanced imaging for accurate placement, cutting procedure times by 22% based on the PROPEL-TAVR pivotal trial involving 450 patients at 35 U.S. and EU centers. Adoption accelerated swiftly, with U.S. implant volumes jumping 68% quarter-over-quarter in Q4 to claim 12% share in the $7.2 billion TAVR sector, according to Millennium Research Group, steadily challenging leaders like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien and Medtronic's Evolut. VitalFlow added $112 million to Q4 revenue, including 55% YoY U.S. growth from broader Medicare eligibility for intermediate-risk cases, 40% increases in Europe following MDR-compliant CE Mark renewal, and promising early momentum in Japan through our Shonin-approved collaboration with Terumo.

Adding to this momentum, the NeuroPulse™ DBS Platform for deep brain stimulation targeting Parkinson's and essential tremor has built strong presence in the $2.5 billion neuromodulation market expanding at 9% annually. Introduced in Q3 2022, it employs adaptive stimulation via machine learning that adjusts pulses in real-time using patient biomarkers, securing FDA PMA approval with MRI-conditional labeling up to 3T fields—a clear edge over Abbott's Infinity and Boston Scientific's Vercise. This translated to $42 million in Q4 sales, up 52% YoY, driven by 60% U.S. procedure expansion from heightened referrals at movement disorder clinics. Overseas, Europe saw 35% growth backed by HTA approvals in Germany and France, while China achieved 25% penetration via our Mindray joint venture, addressing neurology gaps in their vast population.

In diagnostics, the GlucoSense™ CGM Wearable, our factory-calibrated continuous glucose monitor offering 14-day wear and Bluetooth Low Energy smartphone connectivity, has shaken up the $8 billion diabetes management field. Leveraging proprietary bio-impedance for non-invasive trends, it gained 510(k) clearance in Q1 2023 and posted $33 million in Q4 revenue, a 38% YoY rise. This aligns with the post-COVID shift to home monitoring, where our real-world study of 2,500 users showed 30% better adherence. Margins stand at an impressive 75%, aided by our expanded Minnesota manufacturing that trimmed COGS by 18%.

Geographically, the U.S. drove 65% of new product revenue with 42% YoY growth, boosted by the CMS 2024 Physician Fee Schedule's 4.5% outpatient TAVR reimbursement uplift and our Bundled Payments for Care Improvement involvement. Europe contributed 22% with 36% growth, overcoming MDR challenges through proactive compliance unlike some competitors, and tapping the EU4Health €5.3 billion allocation for digital tools. Asia-Pacific, at 10% of new revenue, skyrocketed 55% YoY to $28 million in Q4, accelerated by China's NMPA green channel and India partnerships for cost-effective CGM options. Latin America chipped in $12 million, up 40%, through distributor growth in Brazil and Mexico amid climbing structural heart and diabetes rates at 12% prevalence.

These successes embody our "Innovate-to-Lead" strategy, featuring a $450 million R&D pipeline aiming for five IDE/PMA filings in 2024, such as our robotic-assisted PCI system to compete in the $15 billion robotics space against Intuitive Surgical and Corindus. We've bolstered this with M&A, like the $320 million NeuroDyn acquisition in Q3 for advanced leads technology, delivering immediate 15% IRR accretion. Against rivals, our TAVR share rose 300 basis points ahead of J&J's Ottava, thanks to physician input via the Vitalis Hub app with 15,000 users sharing real-world outcomes.

Forward, we expect new products to power 25-30% of FY 2024 revenue growth, with VitalFlow scaling to $500 million run-rate, NeuroPulse pursuing depression indications via IDE, and GlucoSense aiming for 20% U.S. CGM share. We've countered risks like rare earth inflation in DBS batteries through dual-sourcing and hedged FX with 70% USD revenue exposure.

In essence, these launches are transforming growth at Vitalis, fostering sustainable, high-margin progress in a precision, patient-focused medtech evolution.

Now, let's talk about gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

Our medical devices portfolio—encompassing the CardioVascular segment with premium drug-eluting stents like ZenithFlex, OrthoRebuild joint reconstruction systems rivaling Stryker's Mako robotics, and expanding NeuroStim neuromodulation—demands rigorous cost discipline in a intricate global supply chain.

For Q4, GAAP gross margin hit 66.4%, expanding 210 basis points YoY from 64.3% and 80 basis points sequentially from Q3's 65.6%. Non-GAAP, adjusting for one-time FDA 510(k) remediation on a legacy pacing lead, we achieved 67.2%—our best in over two years, surpassing guidance by 120 basis points through sustained multi-quarter efforts.

Key contributors included favorable product mix adding 150 basis points, with higher-margin consumables and single-use devices now at 58% of revenue, up from 52% YoY. In CardioVascular, ZenithFlex stent kits rose 22% YoY, surpassing capital equipment like imaging cath labs amid elective procedure normalization. OrthoRebuild's robotic implant kits, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci for precision orthopedics, provided 180 basis points lift as U.S. ASC share reached 35%, exceeding our 30% goal.

ASP stability and pricing added 100 basis points, with 2.1% organic ASP growth buoyed by 4.2% hikes on premium neuromodulation leads and CMS IPPS wins, offsetting 1.8% FX drag from a firm USD versus Euro in EMEA.

Manufacturing efficiencies contributed 120 basis points, with Galway, Ireland stent facility and Ankeny, Iowa ortho site at 92% utilization, up from 85%. Yields on bioresorbable scaffolds improved to 98.5% from 96.2% via AI process controls, echoing Boston Scientific's EMBLEM S-ICD advances. Raw materials posed a 50 basis point drag, with medical-grade polycarbonate up 8% YoY on petrochemical swings, though easing from Q1 highs.

By region, U.S. margins rose to 69.1% via Vertically Integrated Manufacturing insourcing 65% of balloon catheter extrusion, cutting Asian reliance. EMEA stayed at 64.8%, balancing MDR-delayed capital with service from 12,000 ZenithFlex labs. APAC jumped 300 basis points to 63.2%, as China volumes rebounded 28% with Hangzhou JV localizing ortho implants under Made-in-China 2025.

On supply chain, resilience persists despite challenges. Safety stock holds 14 weeks for semiconductors in NeuroStim DBS, sterile films, and PEEK—above 10-week target—cushioning Red Sea freight hikes of 15-20%. Turns improved to 4.2x from 3.8x without shortages.

Initiatives include supplier diversification, adding Taiwan and Mexico foundries for ASICs post-2022 shortages like Abbott's MitraClip issues, dropping single-source risk below 10%. Nearshoring advances with $150 million Tijuana facility 40% done for Q4 2025, eyeing 25% North American ortho output to slash leads 35% and dodge 25% Section 301 tariffs. Our SAP-IoT digital twin ensures 95% on-time from DuPont Tyvek and Dow olefins suppliers, up from 88%.

These position us for 67-69% non-GAAP margins in FY 2025 assuming stable resins and no geopolitics spikes. Bolt-on M&A in manufacturing like Integer Holdings machining is in view. Risks like helium for MRI or 4.5% U.S. labor inflation are offset by $300 million OpEx in automation and VIM.

Ultimately, margin gains highlight execution in fixed-cost medtech, with supply fortifications de-risking as electives hit 110% pre-pandemic per Definitive Healthcare.

Moving on to capital equipment versus consumables mix trends.

A pivotal metric illustrating our business resiliency is the capital equipment to consumables revenue mix, core to medtech where capital like our Vitalis Precision Robotic Platform or advanced cath labs builds an installed base fueling annuity recurring from consumables such as single-use catheters, guidewires, stents, and kits.

Q4 revenue totaled $1.25 billion, up 12% organically YoY. Mix: consumables $845 million or 68%, up 18% reported/16% organic—10th straight double-digit quarter; capital $265 million or 21%, +4% organic despite procurement lumpiness; services/other $140 million or 11% from base growth.

FY 2023: consumables $3.2 billion or 66% of $4.85 billion total, up from 62%; capital 23% at $1.12 billion; services 11%. This 66/23/11 beats peers like Intuitive Surgical's ~75% consumables or Boston Scientific's ~60% interventional cardio, with consumables margins up 220 bps to 78% on scale/pricing, capital at 52%.

Mix has shifted deliberately to consumables-led from 58% in FY 2021 post-COVID capital rebound. Drivers: installed base up 22% YoY to 4,200 robotic systems, utilization to 92% in mature markets from 87%, boosting 25% robotic consumables like EndoFlex instruments and FlexiGuide catheters at ~$2,800 ASP. New launches like NeuroFlow aspiration catheters and VisiClear endoscopes sped this; NeuroFlow, FDA-cleared Q2, took 15% thrombectomy share, pulling $120 million consumables akin to Stryker Trevo. Pricing: 3% realization, 5% on consumables premiums; capital ASPs -2% on EM bundling, offset by 85% service attachments.

Regionally: U.S. (52% revenue) consumables 72% from 68%, ASCs now 35% robotic procedures vs 25% 2022, CMS OPPS boosting stents/balloons 20%. EMEA (22%) 65/25, capital strong in Germany/UK post-NHS clearance, consumables +14% despite MDR. APAC/China (20%) capital-heavy 55%, +30% on NMPA Apex sales, consumables +12% with Shanghai JV guidewires for 20% more pull-through by 2025. ROW (6%) consumables +28% on EP kits.

Technical support: $250 million FY 2024 R&D, 60% consumables—SmartConsumables RFID for robotics H1 2024 targeting 5-7% utilization lift like Edwards MITRIS; biodegradable stents Phase III; AI capital software cutting downtime 15%, lifting attachments.

Strategically, razor-razorblade rules: target 70/20/10 by 2025 via 15-20% base growth (ROIC >25%), 90% service, EP M&A like J&J Shockwave. Risks: capital lumpiness, China localization; 4x consumables-capital leverage mitigates.

FY 2024 guide: 11-13% organic, consumables 18-20%, mix to 68% for mid-teens EPS at 25%+ margins.

Next, the impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

These efforts underpinned our 8% organic growth, 210 bps gross margin expansion to 67.8%, and 15% adjusted EBITDA rise to $450 million. Pricing focused on value-based models, mix, and ASPs: 2.8% global ASP growth contributed 1.5 points to organic revenue, third straight sequential gain post-2022 deflation.

Mix shift to premiums: Cardiovascular EvoStent bioresorbables/AI deployment now 35% stent revenue from 22%, ASP $2,800 vs $2,200 legacy, +12% mix benefit on 9% U.S. volumes via TAVR ties like Edwards Sapien.

U.S. (55% device revenue) 3.2% ASP despite 2.5% Medicare IPPS cuts, via IDN contracts (HCA/Kaiser) at 5-7% premiums covering 40% ortho ASPs, buffering ASC shifts. Europe (25%) 1.5% contraction on pacing leads but +1.8% structural heart via NICE/Italy, +15% minimally invasive spine. EM (20%) +4.5% ASPs on Brazil SUS neuro, India Ayushman ortho, China +6% EvoStent post-NMPA vs MicroPort.

FY2024 target 2-3% ASP via Value360 digital twin showing 20-25% OR gains for robotic ortho, like Intuitive da Vinci.

Cost management saved $85 million sequentially toward $350 million FY target, +320 bps to 67.8% despite 7% polymer inflation. Supply dual-sourced 90% resins, -150 bps COGS, 4.2x turns; hedged 70% platinum/iridium -$25 million. Smart Factory automation in Galway/Plymouth: robotic welding cut vascular closure costs $45 to $32, +12% productivity like Abbott Libertas.

SG&A/R&D optimized: $40 million headcount savings, prune 15% early R&D for GLP-1 ortho combos, OpEx to 28% from 31%, digital sales -18% rep costs. Asia localization Singapore -22% freight; U.S. offshore non-GMP -8% prototyping.

Sustainable via 5-6% procedure CAGR to 2028 (Evaluate), total value bundling SaaS monitoring like Medtronic Hugo; ESG recycled titanium -5% materials for EU Green Deal. Risks: PBM/IRA; 45% neuro moat. Guide 2.5% ASP, $400 million savings for double-digit EPS.

Then, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Innovation fuels our $500 billion+ medtech presence, tackling needs in structural heart, neuromodulation, digital therapeutics. Q4 R&D $285 million or 13.2% of $2.16 billion revenue, +18% YoY from $241 million, FYTD $820 million or 12.8% vs industry 8-10%, matching Medtronic/Abbott. Allocates 45% late-stage, 30% early scouting, rest sustaining VeriHeart monitors. Efficiency 4.2x from 3.8x. Footprint: 55% U.S. Minneapolis/SV, 25% Europe Galway, 20% APAC Singapore/Shanghai.

Pipeline: 28 programs (CV 45%, Ortho/Spine 25%, Neuro/Pain 20%, Digital 10%), up from 24 via in-licenses/$150 million biomaterials buy. 12 milestones Q4: 5 submissions, 3 first-in-human, on pace for 45 FY.

Highlights: CV EvoFlow Ultra IDE full enrollment 850 patients/45 sites, 28% less leak vs Sapien 3, 15% better pacemaker rates; FDA IDE supp Q1'24, PMA mid-2026, $1.2B peak U.S. DCB CE Mark, 120 units Germany/Nordics vs Medtronic IN.PACT, $2.5B PAD 9% CAGR.

Ortho/Spine 3D titanium SpineFlex 510(k) submitted, limited U.S. release, 92% fusion vs Stryker 85%; China NMPA/Mindray $1.8B revision.

Neuro closed-loop DBS NeuroSync Pro first patient 300-trial Breakthrough, EEG/ML auto-adjust -40% battery vs Medtronic Percept; Johns Hopkins H2'25 data, 2027 launch $4B 12% market.

Digital CardioPatch 2.0 IDE approved 5,000 vs Apple Watch, Epic/Cerner, NHS 96% sensitivity; $15B digital 25% CAGR, Medicare $50-100/month.

Tailwinds: -12% biomaterial costs reallocating; 60% premium pipeline vs 4.5% Medicare cuts. Partnerships: Siemens JV $50M imaging, NVIDIA edge AI. U.S. 60%, Europe 25% MDR cleared 90%, APAC NMPA fast-tracks.

FY24 $1.15B R&D 12.5%, 6 launches NPV $8.5B. Risks: 8% trial delays, AI guidance; 85% success rate.

Our R&D propels 15-20% growth in precision/outpatient shift.

Then, overall performance highlights and key achievements.

These showcase our diversified strength in CV, ortho, neuromod, structural heart, exceeding guidance via procedures, share gains, pipeline starts.

Q4 revenue $1.28 billion +18% reported/16% organic—strongest Q3 in 5 years, 9th double-digit quarter vs market 8-10%. Adj EPS $0.92 +22%, op margin +250 bps to 28.5%, gross +180 bps to 69.2% on premium consumables/pricing, inflation ease. FCF $285M +25%, $150M buybacks, R&D reinvest.

Franchises: CV 42% $538M +21% organic, 14% procedures, +220 bps U.S. share to 32% (Millennium), Sentinel 35% TAVR adoption -60% stroke, $2.1B backlog +28%. Ortho $320M +15%, robotics 40% revenue, OmniOrtho 92% util like Stryker Mako, intl +22%. Neuro $192M +25%, Infinity DBS 18% U.S. share vs Medtronic. Structural $45M Europe MitraClip-like, 95% adoption.

Regions: U.S. 55% +20% on CMS No Surprises/ASC +12%. Europe 16% €285M equiv MDR 85% renewed. APAC +28% China JV 15% stents Shanghai hub. EM LATAM/India $68M +35% public ortho.

Achievements: FDA 510(k) HugoFlex robotics AI haptics/4K -25% times/30% complications vs da Vinci, 45 placements $750M pipeline. AI CardioAI pacemakers/ICD 92% arrhythmia pred like Abbott Confirm Rx, $200M FY25.

Tailwinds: 5-7% medtech CAGR (BCG), minimally invasive 65% U.S. CV, value-based/digital. R&D $210M 16%, 40 programs bioresorbables/closed-loop pain.

Ops: inventory 128 days from 145, dual titanium/semicon Red Sea hedge. ESG Scope 1 -25% solar U.S. plant EU CSRD.

FY24 14-16% organic CV/robotics-led, $4.2B backlog 3.3x bill, $1.8B net cash M&A like $450M NeuroPulse.

Q4 redefines innovation/execution/patient solutions.

Finally, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Our FY 2024 reiterated: revenue $4.85-4.95B (8-10% reported/9-11% organic), adj EPS $5.80-5.95, gross 66.5% +50 bps. Stress-tested vs McKinsey MedTech.

1. Procedures (60% growth): global 4-5% IQVIA/Leerink. CV 5-6% PCI/TAVR +7% U.S. CRT NovaFlow $10B 12% CAGR. Ortho 4% +3.5% >65 AAOS, OrthoBotix ASC 15% share 25% pen. Neuro/diag 6% DBS +8%, AI ultrasound +10% $50B.

No V-recovery, H2 +2-3% capacity.

2. Regions: U.S. 55% 9-11% flat CMS 2025 IPPS, 340B $150M, 70% private. EMEA 20% 7-9% MDR $80M peak, Germany/UK +10% EuroPulse. APAC 15% 12-14% China 18% NMPA Zenith 3 prods, VBP +15%/-5% price like BSC. EM 10% flat Brazil FX.

3. Pipeline +2%: 5 launches—Q3 CardioScan AI plaque $200M FY25 vs Philips EPIQ; VisiFlex 300 placements $1.2M ASP 25% recur Intuitive; R&D $650M 13.5% 12% productivity Phase III stents, 5G OR $15B robotics.

4. Pricing/mix: net -1-2% U.S. stable/China -8% VBP, +100 bps mix robotics 68% GM vs comm 60%, 85% NTAP neuro.

5. Ops: gross 66.5% -3% mats Galway/Tijuana 85% util, flat FX 2% EUR. OpEx $1.5B 31% SG&A flat R&D +5% AI, 3% merit/5% health. Tax 16.5%, CapEx $350M 7%.

6. Macro: 20% U.S. recession -1% vol JPM, Red Sea +50 bps 60% nearshore, FX -1%. Upside M&A $300M.

Built on procedures/pipeline/rigor, outperform Stryker/Abbott. Update Investor Day Nov.

I will now turn the call over to Maria for a review of our financial results.

Maria Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter. Q4 revenue of $1.28 billion marked 18% reported growth, with full-year at $4.85 billion. Expenses were well-controlled, driving gross margins to 66.4% GAAP and adjusted operating margins to 28.5%. Profitability shone with adjusted EPS of $0.92, up 22% YoY, and robust free cash flow of $285 million supporting buybacks and investments. For FY 2024, we guide revenue to $4.85-4.95 billion, 9-11% organic, EPS $5.80-5.95, with gross margins expanding to 66.5%.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Maria. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of the EvoFlow Ultra TAVR and NeuroSync Pro DBS is progressing well, and we anticipate they will revolutionize structural heart interventions and neuromodulation therapies by improving outcomes and reducing risks.

Our pipeline features 28 programs with key milestones like full IDE enrollment for EvoFlow showing superior leak reduction and first-in-human for NeuroSync's AI-adjusted stimulation. We're on track for multiple approvals and launches, including DCB in PAD and 3D-printed SpineFlex, positioning us for high-acuity growth.

Next, Tom with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Raj. Our commercial team has been instrumental in driving adoption of our products. We are focused on expanding our market presence and enhancing customer engagement.

We've ramped U.S. ASC penetration to 35%, secured IDN contracts covering 40% ortho, and accelerated APAC via JVs in China and India. Physician feedback through Vitalis Hub and outcomes data sharing have boosted shares in TAVR to 12% and DBS to 18%, with backlog at $4.2 billion reflecting strong demand.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Tom. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Lawson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Lawson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On new product launches, can you elaborate on VitalFlow's competitive positioning versus Edwards and Medtronic, especially with U.S. share gains?

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Great question, Mike. VitalFlow's repositionable design and AI imaging have driven 68% QoQ U.S. volume growth to 12% share, outpacing Sapien and Evolut on procedure times reduced 22% per PROPEL-TAVR. Expanded Medicare and our Hub app feedback loops are key differentiators, with global ramp including EU MDR and Japan Terumo partnership fueling $112 million Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Regarding gross margins and supply chain, how sustainable is the 67.2% non-GAAP with Red Sea issues and potential helium shortages?

Maria Chen:
Lisa, our 210 bps expansion reflects mix, pricing, and efficiencies like 92% utilization and AI yields. Supply resilience via 14-week stock, diversified ASICs, and Tijuana nearshoring buffers disruptions. Helium risks for MRI are minor; multi-year automation positions 67-69% FY25 sustainably.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
On consumables mix shifting to 68%, what's the outlook for robotics utilization and capital lumpiness?

Dr. Alex Rivera:
David, consumables at 68% with 16% organic growth leverages our 4,200-system base at 92% utilization, up via new NeuroFlow/VisiClear. FY24 guide 18-20% consumables growth to 70% mix, with selective capital at >25% ROIC hurdle mitigating lumpiness.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
For R&D pipeline, details on NeuroSync Pro's Breakthrough status and potential market?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Sarah, NeuroSync's closed-loop DBS with NeuralNet AI auto-adjusts via EEG, first patient dosed in 300-trial under Breakthrough. Targets $4 billion U.S. PD market +12% growth, -40% battery vs Percept, with H2 2025 data and 2027 launch via Johns Hopkins collab.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
